result.summary:
I implemented internal/jsonx with the specified API unchanged. It provides:
- an ordered Object
- Parse, Stringify, StringifyIndent, Marshal, MarshalIndent
- Decode, Encode
- Opt with Some, Null, IsZero, IsNull, Get
- ParseErrorMessage

**Parse** is a port of V8's json-parser. Error messages match Node 24 exactly:
- Positions are counted in UTF-16 units, with (line L column C).
- The source-context window follows V8's rules, including the special whole-source cases.
- "Unexpected end of JSON input" has no position.
- The non-whitespace-after-JSON message omits " in JSON".

**Object** keeps JS property order. Array-index keys come first in ascending order; other keys keep insertion order, and re-setting a key keeps its position. When parsing duplicate keys, the last value wins but the first position is kept.

**Stringify** matches V8:
- no HTML escaping; U+2028/U+2029 written raw
- escapes are `\b \f \n \r \t` or lowercase `\u00xx`
- numbers use ES Number toString; -0 becomes 0, NaN and ±Inf become null
- the gap is truncated to 10 UTF-16 units
- functions are treated as undefined
- V8's circular-structure TypeError text and the BigInt TypeError are reproduced
- Date toJSON output is used for time.Time

Typed Go values follow encoding/json rules: tags, omitempty, omitzero, `,string`, embedded structs, Marshaler/TextMarshaler. The output of Marshaler and RawMessage is normalized to JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(raw)).

**Decode** follows encoding/json semantics, including the UnmarshalTypeError text. Differences:
- `any` targets receive *Object.
- Opt targets get three states: absent, null, value.

**Added API** (nothing existing changed):
- ParseString, SyntaxError, TypeError
- MustStringify, Quote, AppendQuote, FormatNumber, FormatISOTime, StringifyWithReplacer, Unmarshal
- DeepEqual, CloneValue, IsArrayIndex, OrderKeys, ObjectOf
- Object methods Has, Values, All, Assign, Equal (order-insensitive and used by go-cmp), String, GetString, GetNumber, GetBool, GetObject, GetArray
- Opt methods IsSome, OrElse, Equal

No new dependencies; go-cmp was already in go.mod and is used only by tests. All checks and tests passed in the clone before the sync; I did not re-run them in the main tree.

Neither foundation package existed, so both were written from scratch to the PORTING.md 6.1/6.2/6.4 contract. internal/js and internal/omap were absent from the clone and the main tree, so there was nothing to diff. All 28 files synced with no conflicts or rejections.

internal/js:
- UTF-16 string model over Go UTF-8: each invalid byte counts as 1 unit and reads as U+FFFD; a lone surrogate from a slice boundary becomes U+FFFD.
- String methods: slice/substring/charCodeAt/codePointAt, indexOf/lastIndexOf, split, pad, trim, byte/UTF-16 offset conversion, CompareUTF16, case mapping, normalize, localeCompare, plus the JS whitespace regex class.
- Numbers: Number::toString and radix toString. Radix output is a V8 port; explicit float64 conversions stop arm64 FMA fusion. Also toFixed/toPrecision (exact, half-up), Math.round, parseInt (V8 algorithm), parseFloat, Number(), ArrayIndex and en-US toLocaleString.
- Dates: Date.now, toISOString, toLocaleString, and a full V8 DateParser port for Date.parse.
- URI: encodeURI(Component) and decodeURI(Component).
- TextDecoder: exact port of the Node 24 UTF-8 fast path, including its BOM quirk.
- Errors: JSError, TypeError/RangeError/URIError/SyntaxError, and ErrorString with the AbortError/TimeoutError mapping.
- Sleep follows the setTimeout clamp and returns context.Cause on abort. Platform/Arch map Go names to Node names.

Bugs found and fixed while comparing against node vectors:
- CompareUTF16 treated an invalid byte and U+FFFD as unequal.
- URI decode bounds check was wrong, and it rejected a valid %EF%BF%BD.
- Radix toString last digits were off on arm64 (FMA).
- lastIndexOf(empty, mid-surrogate position) returned the wrong index.
- parseInt radix 36 was wrong on large values.
- TextDecoder BOM handling diverged across streamed chunks.

internal/omap:
- Map and Set with JS iteration semantics: tombstones with deferred compaction, so deletes and adds during a loop behave as in JS.
- Map JSON uses JS object key order (array-index keys ascending first, then insertion order) with no HTML escaping. Unmarshal inserts keys in Object.keys order, and the last duplicate value wins.

The node vector generators are kept in internal/js/testdata with a README and reproduce the vectors byte for byte. The /tmp/jsvec scratch directory was deleted. No go.mod changes and no git write commands.

I also ran a temporary differential fuzz against node v24.21.0 on the final code and removed it before syncing. It had 0 mismatches across: 150k+ random JSON.parse/stringify/indent cases, every UTF-16 code unit (77,824 quote cases), 600k random doubles, 160k invalid-UTF-8 byte inputs to Parse (about 900 of them truncated surrogate prefixes), and 160k raw-byte Quote cases. Node's UTF-8 decoder turns those bytes into three U+FFFD. This form is what lets JSON escapes like "\ud83d" round-trip byte-exactly, and Node never writes such bytes. The Stringify depth limit is a fixed 6185 nested containers. In V8 the limit depends on the caller's stack (I measured 5585 to 6203 on node v24), so inputs nested between about 5600 and 6200 levels can behave differently from TS.

Clone, CloneValue, DeepEqual, Object.Equal and Decode into recursive struct types still recurse. Now that Parse accepts any depth, a document nested several million levels deep could still overflow the goroutine stack in those helpers.
Object.Set does not emulate the JS `__proto__` assignment setter: Set("__proto__", v) always creates an own property. JSON.parse and spread semantics are correct.

Decode keeps encoding/json rules: a case-insensitive key match is the fallback, and []byte uses base64. JS is case-sensitive and stringifies Uint8Array differently. Section 5.5 of PORTING.md asks for encoding/json semantics, so I left this as is.

Every PORTING.md 5.1 item exists with the specified signature: Object and its methods, Parse, ParseErrorMessage, Stringify, StringifyIndent, Marshal, MarshalIndent, Decode, Encode, and Opt with Some, Null, IsZero, IsNull and Get. The tree only uses the jsonx symbols that exist. No TODOs or placeholders were found. The untyped parse/stringify core already matched node exactly, so I fixed the following real gaps:

1. **Fatal crash on deeply nested input (parse.go).** Parse was recursive, so 10M '[' characters overflowed the goroutine stack and killed the process. Node returns "Unexpected end of JSON input" there. I rewrote the parser to use an explicit stack, as V8 does. Error messages and positions are unchanged; the fuzz run confirms this.

2. **No limit on Stringify nesting (stringify.go).** Stringify now returns a new `*RangeError` ("Maximum call stack size exceeded", `Name()` "RangeError") beyond 6185 nested containers. That is the depth node reaches from a shallow stack, and it also prevents a Go stack overflow. Decode's internal re-marshal for json.Unmarshaler targets uses a separate safety limit of 100000 levels instead. That value was chosen after a 1M-level test overflowed under `-race`.

3. **StringifyWithReplacer lacked cycle detection.** A cyclic value recursed until the process crashed. It now fails with V8's exact circular-structure TypeError, using index keys for array elements as V8 does, and it applies the depth limit.

4. **Large integers were not printed as JS numbers.** Go integers beyond ±2^53 printed their exact digits; now they print as the nearest double (math.MaxInt64 becomes 9223372036854776000). json.Number now gives JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(token)).

5. **Truncated surrogate bytes decoded differently from Node (utf16.go).** Input like ED A0 or ED A0 41 produced one U+FFFD where Node's WHATWG decoder produces two.

6. **Pointer-receiver MarshalJSON/MarshalText was skipped on values that are not addressable.** Examples are a struct passed by value, map values, and values held in interfaces. This differs from encoding/json on purpose, so that Stringify(x) and Stringify(&x) give the same bytes. Without it, a value-typed omap.Map field would encode as {}.

doc.go now describes the nesting, integer and marshaler rules. Scratch files in /tmp/jsonx-fparity and the workspace clone were removed.

I ported all three foundation packages to Go and synced them to the main tree. They only use modules already in go.mod (x/net/idna, x/text, x/sys, x/term), and go.mod is unchanged.

**internal/hostedgit** (hosted-git-info@9.0.3)
- **URL parser**: a full WHATWG URL parser, because hosted-git-info parses every git URL with `new URL()`.
  - Type `URL` with `NewURL`, `NewURLWithBase` and `URLCanParse`. It has all the getters and setters (setters change the URL in place, as the spec says) plus `String` and `ToJSON`.
  - Supports IPv4 (hex and octal forms), IPv6, opaque hosts, and IDNA via x/net/idna.
  - Behaviour matches Node 24 (ada 4.0.0): ASCII hosts are only lowercased, and a space before `?` or `#` in an opaque path becomes `%20`.
- **API**: `FromUrl(giturl, *Options) *GitHost`, `FromUrlChecked` (also returns the TypeError TS throws), `FromManifest`, `ParseUrl`, and every `GitHost` method.
  - Methods: Hash, Ssh, Sshurl, Browse, BrowsePath, BrowseFile, Docs, Bugs, Https, Git, Shortcut, Path, Tarball, File, Edit, GetDefaultRepresentation, ToString, String.
  - `GitHost` fields carry JSON tags that match `JSON.stringify`.
- **Parity**: the host templates and URL extraction port lib/ exactly, including TS quirks marked `// TS parity:`. For example, a null user prints as "null", and a github `/tree` URL with no committish gets the committish "undefined".

**internal/lockfile** (proper-lockfile@4.1.2): Lock, LockSync, Unlock, UnlockSync, Check, CheckSync and CleanupOnExit. It includes the retry module, Node-style error messages, and the stale / update / mtime-precision behaviour. It works alongside a running TS pi: I checked it manually against TS proper-lockfile.

**internal/ansi** (chalk@6.0.0 plus its bundled supports-color): output is byte-identical to chalk, as checked against node-generated vectors.

**Checks**: gofmt, gopls, build, vet (darwin, windows and linux), `go test` and `go test -race` all pass for the three packages, including a re-run in the main tree after the sync.

**Decisions for you**: two NEEDS_DECISION files were written.
- `lockfile.CleanupOnExit` needs registering with the exit hook; nothing calls it yet.
- NO_COLOR has no effect, because chalk 6 ignores it and pi never reads it, although PORTING.md lists it.

The remaining deviations are listed in gaps_remaining.

result.summary:
I ported quickjs-wasi 3.6.2's JS glue (dist/index.js and dist/wasi-shim.js) to Go as package internal/quickjs. It runs the embedded, unmodified quickjs.wasm on wazero v1.12.0. Build, vet and gofmt are clean, and all tests pass, including under -race.

How it works:
- All VMs share one wazero runtime, created once with CloseOnContextDone. Host functions find their VM through the call context.
- Each wasm export has its own pool of call engines, so host callbacks can safely call back into the VM.
- After the first trap, context abort, out-of-bounds access or malloc failure, the VM is permanently failed. Methods that return errors report that failure, and Err() exposes it. Cancelling the context surfaces as a *WasmError that satisfies errors.Is(err, context.Canceled).
- Calling Dispose from inside a host callback is safe. The instance is closed once the outermost call returns.
- Strings use WTF-8, so guest strings with lone surrogates round-trip exactly. TextDecoder semantics (BOM stripping, U+FFFD replacement) match node.

Public surface covers everything pi's codemode worker uses, plus most of the TS API:
- create/restore with options: wasm, wasi overrides, memoryLimit, maxStackSize, interrupt handler, unhandled-rejection handler, module loader, intrinsics, timezone
- evalCode/compile/evalBytecode/executePendingJobs
- handles with the full is*/introspection set, property access and descriptors, proxies, conversions, consume/dup
- dump and hostToHandle
- functions (named, ephemeral, unregister), withScope/escape, export/import handles
- promises (newPromise/Deferred, resolvePromise as a channel, promiseThenRaw, markPromiseHandled), callFunction/construct, newError, GC and memory usage
- snapshot, serialize and deserialize with byte-exact headers and the TS error messages
- the WASI shim with merged user overrides

Error messages are ported verbatim from TS. testdata/gen_vectors.mjs regenerates the parity vectors (needs QUICKJS_WASI_DIR). Scratch files under /tmp were deleted. No git write commands were run and go.mod was not touched.

gaps_remaining: Native extensions (the TS `extensions` option) are not ported. Snapshots that need extensions are rejected, using the TS missing-extension error text.
HostToHandle does not convert a host Promise to a guest promise (TS hostToHandle does). Use NewPromise/Deferred instead.
There are no TS-style default filename arguments. EvalCode and Compile take an explicit filename.
wazero trap message texts (stack exhaustion, unreachable) differ from V8 WebAssembly.RuntimeError texts. Name and kind (WasmError, Name "RuntimeError") match.

Behaviour differs from TS when there is no maxStackSize and recursion runs deep. TS gets a V8 RangeError from the wasm frames; Go gets a wazero trap that permanently fails the VM (sticky WasmError). A nested-call trap or a malloc failure also becomes a sticky VM failure, where TS would throw into the guest or the host. With MaxStackSize set (codemode sets it), overflow is a catchable guest RangeError in both.
Go errors returned from host callbacks carry no host (JS) stack trace, so the error's stack in the guest has only the guest frames.

The host timezone comes from Go tzdata (time.Local), not ICU. Historical LMT offsets can differ by tzdata version: for example, node/ICU gives Europe/Amsterdam pre-1900 as +0:17, a Brussels link. Modern offsets match.

The random_get QuotaExceededError text comes from node v24 ('The requested length exceeds 65,536 bytes'). Older node versions word it differently. QuickJS core never requests more than 65536 bytes, so in practice it is unreachable without the crypto extension.
Nothing imports internal/quickjs yet: the codemode/runtime Go files are still stubs, so the worker.ts flow is covered only by TestCodemodeWorkerFlow inside this package.
